label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Hey Mikaela, yep we did, started on 21 Sept after mating had started. We’ve got 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We skip the Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday arvo milkings, so four once-a-days a week. Still a 5.15 start every morning unfortunately!

Honestly, milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. The rep had told us to expect 8–10% so it’s not as bad as we’d braced for, but it’s still a decent hit and worth doing your own sums on. That’s just our comparison so far, not a promise that’s where we’ll end up.

Cells did jump. We were around 110,000 and went up to about 180,000 for the first three weeks. They’ve come back to around 135,000 now, so better, but still a bit higher than where we started.

The bad bit is we had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped arvo and we didn’t spot it till the next morning. She lost a quarter. That really knocked us around and I don’t want to gloss over it. You have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days or it bites you.

On the other hand the lame cows are way down. We’ve got 4 on the lame list now compared with 11 this time last year, and it’s a 1.8 km walk to our back paddocks. The cows came round quicker than I thought too. About four days of bellowing at the gate and then they were fine.

The hours have made a huge difference to us. First skipped Sunday arvo Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years! Kieran said it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October, which probably tells you plenty. And if Tom’s knees are as bad as you say, I reckon the arvos off will help more than anything.

Honestly I wouldn’t go back, the hours alone are worth the 6% for us. But I wouldn’t want to talk you into it either, especially after that heifer. Have a look at your own numbers and talk it through with your vet.

Come and have a look at our shed rosters and numbers at the field day on the 19th if you’re there. Or just ring me if you want a yarn, much easier than texting!
